players.product: Electron small launch and Neutron medium-lift launch vehicle (in development)

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab 10-K: 2025 revenue was $601.8 million, a year-on-year increase of approximately 38%; Space Systems revenue was $402.8 million (+30%, primarily spacecraft manufacturing growth) and Launch Services revenue $199.0 million (+59%) with 21 launch missions completed versus 16 in 2024; gross margin 34.4%; approximately 47% of 2025 revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. government.
quarterly_data.figure: $601.8 million (38%); Space Systems $402.8 million; Launch Services $199.0 million; 21 launch missions; 47%

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab 10-K: revenue per launch was $8.5 million in 2025 versus $7.8 million in 2024, while cost per launch fell to $4.8 million from $5.7 million, driven by efficiencies of scale. Backlog increased from $1,067.0 million to $1,847.3 million ($1,371.7 million space systems, $475.6 million launch services), including the SDA Tranche 3 contract and the GEOST acquisition; approximately 37% is expected to be recognized within 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue per launch $8.5 million; cost per launch $4.8 million; backlog $1,847.3 million (37% within 12 months)

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab 10-K: in 2025 Electron was the second most frequently launched orbital rocket; Launch Complex 1 in Mahia, New Zealand (two pads, Pad A and Pad B) is capable of supporting up to 120 launches per year, LC-2 at NASA's Wallops Flight Facility is operational and LC-3 at Wallops is being developed to receive and integrate Neutron launch vehicles; Neutron's first launch was targeted for Q4 2026 at the time of the 10-K. Capital expenditures were $156.3 million in 2025 and Rocket Lab had over 2,600 full-time permanent employees.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 120 launches per year; capex $156.3 million; over 2,600 employees

quarterly_data.signal: Rocket Lab 10-K: under the February 2022 procurement agreement with MDA Corporation to design and manufacture 17 spacecraft buses, projected delivery dates for certain deliverables will be later than originally set, partly due to delays in Rocket Lab's supply chain; MDA is potentially entitled to claim liquidated damages, Rocket Lab is similarly entitled to claim liquidated damages against certain suppliers that contributed to the delays, and the net amount cannot yet be determined.
